This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.
This is an application for bail.

The appellant-petitioner Susil Digal @ Sushil has been convicted under sections 376(2)(i)/
376(2)(f)/ 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life and to pay a fine of Rs.20,000/- (rupees twenty thousand), in default to undergo R.I. for a further period of six months for each of the offences by the learned Additional Sessions -cum- Judge, Special Court under POCSO Act, Bhubaneswar in T.R. Case No.93 of 2016.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 20.05.2016 and the informant (P.W.1), who is the mother of the victim, has not supported the prosecution case fully, for which she was declared hostile.

Learned counsel further submits that the victim's evidence that rape was committed on her for four times is not getting any corroboration from the evidence of Susil Digal @ Sushil vs State Of Odisha on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118927864/
1 the doctor (P.W.10), and therefore, there is good chance of success in the appeal and balance of convenience is in his favour.

entities.text: Susil Digal @ Sushil vs State Of Odisha on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the bail application of the petitioner may be favourably considered.

Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the prayer for bail and placed the evidence of the victim (P.W.2), who was aged about ten years at the time of deposition and studying in class-VII and she has also categorically stated that the petitioner, who was her father, committed rape on her for four times.
Learned counsel for the State also placed the evidence of the doctor (P.W.10).

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the relationship of the petitioner and the victim and the manner in which the crime has been committed,
particularly, the age of the victim, we are not inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
The I.A. accordingly stands rejected.
(S.K. Sahoo)

Judge  (Chittaranjan Dash)
